column3: No music played in the Nameless Tavern in Sentinel, and indeed there was very little sound, except for discreet, cautious murmurs of conversation, the soft pad of the barmaid's feet on stone, and the delicate slurping of the regular patrons, tongues lapping at their flagons, eyes focused on nothing at all.
If anyone were less otherwise occupied, the sight of the young Redguard woman in a fine black velvet cape might have aroused surprise.
As it were, the strange figure, out of place in an underground cellar so modest it had no sign, blended into the shadows.
The stout, middle-aged man with a face older than his years looked up and nodded.
The young woman took the seat next to him.
My name is Haballa, she said, and pulled out a small bag of gold, placing it next to his mug.
Sure it be, snarled Jomic, and met her eyes again.
She did not turn away, but merely asked, "Is it safe to talk here?"

No one cares about nobody else's problems but their own here.
600	1	You could take off your cuirass and dance bare-breasted on the table, and no one'd even spit, the man smiled.

The truth is, I only want someone... removed, for a while.
500	0	Not harmed, you understand, and that's why I need a professional.
1500	0	You come highly recommended.
